seeds.optional_extra_seeds_rule: run only if compute allows, and then for every method

budget.unit: supervised (loss-bearing) response tokens under the Student tokenizer; prompt tokens are masked from the loss and logged separately
budget.beta_round_rule: n_round * mean token length of verified trajectories
budget.probe_budget_note: b = one epoch over a 50-trajectory group at effective batch 8 (= ceil(50/8) = 7 steps), same regime as one training round
budget.l_emp_groups: 5 token-length quintile bins of the eligible pool at S_0; 50 trajectories sampled per bin with seed 363636
budget.pool_token_stats: reports/task5/pool_token_stats.json (Student tokenizer; response mean 227.13, with prompt mean 359.6)
budget.L_bar_source: reports/task5/pool_token_stats.json (480 verified trajectories of the preliminary pool, Student tokenizer)
budget.pool_requirement: Task 6 official D_pool trajectory pool must cover >= 1000 problems (5 x n_round with n_cap = 1); otherwise revise via config v2 before training
budget.b1_exception: B1 trains on the full pool once per round (reference, higher cost), not budget-matched

selection.b3_rule: per problem: shortest correct trajectory (Student tokenizer), tie -> smallest trajectory_id; shuffle problems once with seed; walk that order across rounds, each round continuing where the previous stopped and filling until beta_round; no trajectory repeats
selection.retention_r_source: TiC-LM (ACL 2025, arXiv 2504.02107) Sec. 5-6.1: alpha_t = 1/2 recommended (half budget current data, half replay)
selection.b4_rule: rank all eligible trajectories once by L_proxy(tau | S_0) descending, tie_break applied; walk that ranking across rounds, each round continuing with the remaining trajectories and filling until beta_round; a trajectory skipped by n_cap in a round stays available for later rounds; no trajectory repeats; identical across training seeds
selection.allow_reselect_note: applies to B2, B5 and the ablation; the B3 and B4 schedules never repeat a trajectory

training.batch_size_note: effective batch size (per-device x gradient accumulation)
training.adapter_across_rounds: continue the same LoRA adapter from S_t; optimizer state re-initialized each round
training.hyperparameter_source: QLoRA (Dettmers et al., 2023, arXiv 2305.14314) Appendix: LoRA on all linear layers, dropout 0.1 for models up to 13B, constant LR schedule, Adam beta2 0.999, max grad norm 0.3

evaluation.answer_verifier: scripts/answer_utils.py:evaluate_output (invalid_format counts as incorrect; format compliance reported separately)

sample_record.question: Mimi picked up 2 dozen seashells on the beach. Kyle found twice as many shells as Mimi and put them in his pocket. Leigh grabbed one-third of the shells that Kyle found. How many seashells did Leigh have?
sample_record.reasoning_trace:
1. First, determine how many seashells Mimi picked up. Since she picked up 2 dozen seashells, and there are 12 seashells in a dozen, Mimi picked up \( 2 \times 12 = 24 \) seashells.
   
2. Next, calculate how many seashells Kyle found. Kyle found twice as many shells as Mimi, so Kyle found \( 24 \times 2 = 48 \) seashells.

3. Then, find out how many seashells Leigh grabbed. Leigh grabbed one-third of the shells that Kyle found, so Leigh grabbed \( \frac{48}{3} = 16 \) seashells.
sample_record.raw_generation:
REASONING:
1. First, determine how many seashells Mimi picked up. Since she picked up 2 dozen seashells, and there are 12 seashells in a dozen, Mimi picked up \( 2 \times 12 = 24 \) seashells.
   
2. Next, calculate how many seashells Kyle found. Kyle found twice as many shells as Mimi, so Kyle found \( 24 \times 2 = 48 \) seashells.

3. Then, find out how many seashells Leigh grabbed. Leigh grabbed one-third of the shells that Kyle found, so Leigh grabbed \( \frac{48}{3} = 16 \) seashells.

ANSWER:
Leigh had 16 seashells.

compute_nll.help:
usage: compute_nll.py [-h] --tag TAG [--adapter ADAPTER] --out OUT
                      [--batch-size BATCH_SIZE] [--limit LIMIT] [--pool POOL]
                      [--model MODEL] [--revision REVISION]
                      [--dtype {auto,bf16,fp32,fp16}]

Score every verified pool trajectory under a Student checkpoint (one forward pass, no backward).

Per trajectory tau (trajectory tokens only, the end-of-turn token excluded):
  nll_sum    = sum_t -log p(tau_t | x, tau_<t)
  ell        = nll_sum / n_tokens            (length-normalized NLL; input of L_proxy, config "learnability")
  brier_sum  = sum_t || pi_t - onehot(tau_t) ||^2
               (Brier residual; stored so the LARK score, arXiv 2605.30651 Eq. 7, can be computed
                later without another pass. Exploratory, not part of the frozen L_proxy.)

L_proxy itself is not computed here: it needs ell over the whole pool (median / IQR rule) and
is derived in the analysis step.

--pool defaults to the official pool v1 (trajectory/pool/pool_v1_verified.jsonl). The Task 5 smoke test
scored the preliminary pool; reproduce it with --pool trajectory/pool/batch_100_teacher_verified.jsonl.

Usage (from experiments/week2September/manual/):
  python scripts/compute_nll.py --tag S0 --out reports/task5/smoke_test/nll_pool_S0.jsonl       --pool trajectory/pool/batch_100_teacher_verified.jsonl
  python scripts/compute_nll.py --tag S1_seed13 --adapter <adapter_dir>       --out reports/task5/smoke_test/nll_pool_S1_seed13.jsonl --pool trajectory/pool/batch_100_teacher_verified.jsonl

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --tag TAG
  --adapter ADAPTER
  --out OUT
  --batch-size BATCH_SIZE
  --limit LIMIT
  --pool POOL           verified pool to score (default: pool v1)
  --model MODEL         override the Student model (pipeline tests only;
                        default: config student.model)
  --revision REVISION   revision for --model
  --dtype {auto,bf16,fp32,fp16}

train_round.help:
usage: train_round.py [-h] --seed SEED --train-set TRAIN_SET --adapter-dir
                      ADAPTER_DIR [--init-adapter INIT_ADAPTER]
                      [--micro-batch MICRO_BATCH] [--epochs EPOCHS] [--lr LR]
                      [--no-gradient-checkpointing] [--pool POOL]
                      [--model MODEL] [--revision REVISION]
                      [--dtype {auto,bf16,fp32,fp16}]

Train one round of the Student with LoRA: S_t + B_t -> S_{t+1}.

Hyperparameters come from config/experiment_config.json "training" (LoRA r/alpha/dropout/targets,
AdamW, constant lr, no warmup, max_grad_norm, effective batch, 1 epoch, max_seq_len,
completion-only loss). Effective batch = --micro-batch x gradient accumulation.

Loss: token-level mean over all supervised (response) tokens of the effective batch;
prompt tokens are masked. Seeds: torch seed (LoRA init, dropout) = data order seed = --seed.

Pool: the trajectories are looked up in the pool named by the train set ("pool", checked against
"pool_sha256"), so the Task 5 smoke-test train sets still resolve to the preliminary pool; train sets
without that field use --pool (default: official pool v1).

Outputs:
  <adapter-dir>/                 LoRA adapter (safetensors) + tokenizer files
  <adapter-dir>/train_log.json   per-step loss, tokens, time; totals; config used

Usage (from experiments/week2September/manual/):
  python scripts/train_round.py --seed 13       --train-set reports/task5/smoke_test/train_set_seed13.json       --adapter-dir models/smoke/student_ckpt_001_smoke_seed13

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --seed SEED
  --train-set TRAIN_SET
                        JSON with trajectory_ids (select_smoke_train_set.py)
  --adapter-dir ADAPTER_DIR
  --init-adapter INIT_ADAPTER
                        continue from an existing adapter (round t > 0)
  --micro-batch MICRO_BATCH
  --epochs EPOCHS       default: config training.epochs_per_round
  --lr LR               default: config training.learning_rate
  --no-gradient-checkpointing
  --pool POOL           pool for train sets without a 'pool' field (default:
                        official pool v1)
  --model MODEL         override the Student model (pipeline tests only;
                        default: config student.model)
  --revision REVISION   revision for --model
  --dtype {auto,bf16,fp32,fp16}

eval_student.help:
usage: eval_student.py [-h] --tag TAG [--adapter ADAPTER] --out OUT
                       [--summary SUMMARY] [--split {dev,test}]
                       [--backend {hf,vllm}] [--batch-size BATCH_SIZE]
                       [--gpu-memory-utilization GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION]
                       [--limit LIMIT] [--model MODEL] [--revision REVISION]
                       [--dtype {auto,bf16,fp32,fp16}]

Evaluate a Student checkpoint on D_dev or D_test with the frozen evaluation protocol.

Protocol (config/experiment_config.json "evaluation"): prompt v1, greedy decoding,
max_new_tokens 512, answers scored by answer_utils.evaluate_output
(invalid_format counts as incorrect; format compliance reported separately).

Greedy is enforced explicitly: the Qwen generation_config ships sampling defaults and
repetition_penalty 1.05, which would otherwise still apply under do_sample=False.

Also records lenient_correct (last number anywhere in the output, format ignored): the registered
secondary metric of T7-5, always reported with strict accuracy and format compliance. Accuracy per
capability is added on D_dev, over the problems with manual labels.

Backends:
  hf    transformers generate (default; used by the Task 5 smoke test)
  vllm  vLLM with the same greedy settings; needs a bf16 GPU (L4/A100). A LoRA adapter is merged into a
        temporary model directory first, exactly as the hf backend merges it before generating.

Output (resumable: problem_ids already in --out are skipped):
  --out           one JSON line per problem
  --summary       accuracy, format compliance, output length, timing, memory

Usage (from experiments/week2September/manual/):
  python scripts/eval_student.py --tag S0 --out reports/task5/smoke_test/eval_S0_dev.jsonl
  python scripts/eval_student.py --tag S1_seed13 --adapter <adapter_dir>       --out reports/task5/smoke_test/eval_S1_dev_seed13.jsonl
  python scripts/eval_student.py --split test --backend vllm --tag S1 --adapter <adapter_dir> --out <out.jsonl>

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --tag TAG             checkpoint label, e.g. S0 or S1_seed13
  --adapter ADAPTER     LoRA adapter directory (omit for S_0)
  --out OUT
  --summary SUMMARY     default: <out>.summary.json
  --split {dev,test}
  --backend {hf,vllm}
  --batch-size BATCH_SIZE
                        default: 16 for hf, 200 for vllm
  --gpu-memory-utilization GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION
                        vllm backend only
  --limit LIMIT         first N problems only (pipeline tests)
  --model MODEL         override the Student model (pipeline tests only;
                        default: config student.model)
  --revision REVISION   revision for --model
  --dtype {auto,bf16,fp32,fp16}
